clue.text: Breeding a hybrid for shading

parts.note: a cross is a hybrid animal or plant

explanation.surface: A horticulturist breeds a hybrid to get a particular shading of colour.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives the pieces in the reverse order: 'Breeding a hybrid' is hatching a cross, read with the cross first.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine parallel lines drawn across each other are an artist's way of adding tone to a drawing.

clue.text: Salvation Army:?

parts.note: the clue asks for another name for an army fighting for salvation: the Christian body on earth, struggling against evil

explanation.definitionFit: Theologians call the living members of the Christian body, at war with sin, the fighting church on earth.

clue.text: Your Honour to command:

definitions.meaning: an honour such as a knighthood is conferred as membership of a chivalric body, e.g. of the Garter

explanation.definitionFit: An honour is membership of a chivalric society, and to command someone is to instruct them.

clue.text: Vegetable to get in barns 'perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters that follow are only one possible arrangement, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tells a farmhand to bring the vegetables into the barns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the ten letters of GET IN and BARNS; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A long green pod eaten whole is a common garden vegetable.

clue.text: A pine fruit is without it, in flower

parts.note: a cone is the fruit of a pine tree
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pine cone appears to lack something, set among flowers.

explanation.definitionFit: Monkshood or wolfsbane, a poisonous plant with hooded blooms, is a garden flower.

clue.text: The noted fall of that: revolting Jack?

definitions.text: The noted fall of that: revolting Jack?

parts.words: The noted fall of that: revolting Jack
parts.note: a musical close, a fall in notes, read playfully as belonging to Jack Cade, who led the revolt of 1450

explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade led a popular revolt in Kent in 1450, so the 'revolting Jack' is Cade; 'noted' means set to musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A falling close in a melody, here punned on the name of the rebel Jack Cade.

clue.text: Some fair maid of Sapper

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pretty young woman appears in the works of the writer Sapper.
explanation.walkthrough: Sapper wrote the Bulldog Drummond thrillers, whose villainess is Irma Peterson.
explanation.definitionFit: Irma Peterson is the female villain in the Bulldog Drummond stories by the author Sapper.

clue.text: German with 'a French face."." describes, part of speech

dial is slang for a face

explanation.surface: A phrase about a German with a French face is analysed as a part of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is an adjective, so the definition is 'describes part of speech': it describes a gerund, a verbal noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to the gerund, the verbal noun ending in -ing that grammarians class as a part of speech.

clue.text: Nourishing but monotonous if that's all for dinner

definitions.text: Nourishing but monotonous if that's all for dinner

parts.words: Nourishing but monotonous if that's all for dinner
parts.note: a healthy brown loaf which, if it made up the entire evening meal, would be dull eating

explanation.definitionFit: A loaf made from unrefined flour is wholesome, but a dinner of nothing else is tedious.

clue.text: Like an 'old Promenader in the coppice '

definitions.meaning: concertgoers at the London Proms stood beneath the baton of the conductor Sir Henry Wood

explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are a London summer concert season; Sir Henry Wood conducted them for nearly fifty years.
explanation.definitionFit: Proms audiences played under the conductor Henry Wood, and a coppice is a thicket of small trees and scrub.

clue.text: Can be deadly slow this time of year

definitions.meaning: a funeral ..., the dead ..., is played at a slow pace
the month in which spring begins

explanation.definitionFit: A dead march is slow funeral music, and the third month is a time of the year.

clue.text: Shepherd one found in the harvest field.

parts.note: a cornfield is harvested, so corn stands for the field
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A shepherd is discovered out in a field at harvest time.
explanation.walkthrough: Corin is the old shepherd in Shakespeare's As You Like It.
explanation.definitionFit: Corin is the elderly shepherd of the Forest of Arden in Shakespeare's As You Like It.

clue.text: Draughty houses

parts.note: not buildings full of cold air but public houses that serve beer on draught

explanation.definitionFit: Pubs and taverns serve draught beer, so they are houses of draught.

clue.text: Indigo, if one has ' the money

definitions.text: Indigo, if one has ' the money

parts.words: Indigo, if one has ' the money
parts.note: a blue dye plant, with the joke that indigo sounds like 'in dough', slang for being well off

explanation.definitionFit: A West Indian shrub yields a deep blue dye, the source of indigo.

clue.text: Concert in C may be for these circles

explanation.surface: A concert in the key of C might suit a particular musical society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges CONCERT IN C; 'for' is a link. The definition is adjectival: circles sharing one centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Circles drawn round a common centre point are described as sharing a centre.

clue.text: That may be changed-or silenced?

definitions.meaning: read whimsically as able to be muted

explanation.definitionFit: Something changeable can be altered, and the word playfully splits as 'mute-able', able to be silenced.

clue.text: Ostrogoth of the round Greek Order

O is round in shape

explanation.definitionFit: Theodoric the Great was king of the Ostrogoths, a Germanic people, and ruled Italy.

clue.text: The Number One vice

parts.note: not the worst sin but the failing of being obsessed with number one, oneself

explanation.definitionFit: Self-absorption is the fault of putting yourself, number one, first.

clue.text: Unblasted islands

parts.note: a Caribbean island group named as being on the side sheltered from the wind

explanation.definitionFit: The sheltered side, away from the wind, is never blasted, giving the name of a Caribbean island chain.

clue.text: He can perhaps beat Red in dialectic

definitions.text: He can perhaps beat Red in dialectic

indicators.note: perhaps says the two words are just one possible arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: A man may outargue a Communist in a philosophical argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges BEAT RED; the whole clue is also the definition, since a skilled arguer might beat a Marxist at dialectic.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who argues formally in public disputes might outdo a Marxist in argument.

clue.text: Saint with a 'musically lofty 'reputation ?.

parts.note: the patron saint of music, who in Dryden's ode raised music heavenward by drawing an angel down

clue.text: This sea change, changes achieved knots

clue.text: Implore Puck to return Charon's toll.

clue.text: What was Anna to him ?. 'Not much :

clue.text: Famous old fighter down on the canvas
